exact_target.scope: For every odd q>=5, explicit nonsquare-endpoint matrices generate the index-two extension L2(q) over PSL4(q), with actual rank-three IP. method: The dimension-four form alternative combines with a monomial torus obstruction, transvection equations and the self-centralizing simple socle. The upper bound also applies to PSU4(q)<=G<=PGU4(q). A uniform matrix template generates SU4(q) for q=1 mod4 and has projective IP whenever the middle order is q^2-1 or q^2+1, using two auxiliary forms and a regular-torus bound. An elliptic primitive-character sieve and 406 independently checked field witnesses prove parameter existence for every odd q=1 mod4; characteristic three uses the rational curve from phase twelve. A second sphere template, twisted norm curve and primitive sieve cover q=3 mod4, q>=7, with 1699 independently checked exceptional parameter records and full q7/q11 finite group certificates. Together these prove maximum rank four for every odd q>=5. The failed-IP control remains.

Prime-field triangular generators plus one field parameter produce every elementary root. A symmetric-form intersection inside the known triangular subgroup has exactly 4p elements, giving the full rank-four IP without an orthogonal subgroup classification.

A common four-matrix template and an auxiliary semilinear involution reduce the two maximal-parabolic intersection to a binary orthogonal group. Explicit vertex eigenvalues control arbitrary projective similitude multipliers in both congruence branches.

The common cocycle/complement theorem replaces the additive-kernel generation steps in the linear and unitary constructions. Independent factors work over every field and arbitrary block sizes; the coupled unitary criterion holds for odd q>=5 and has an explicit proper-complement counterexample at q=3. Full projected image, ambient roots and IP remain separate.
